fatal_flaws.claim: §4.11: tenant HTML is edge-cached by setting `cloudflare-cdn-cache-control: public, max-age=86400, ...` plus `vary: Accept-Encoding` — 'ONLY this. Never Cookie. Never User-Agent.'
fatal_flaws.why_wrong: Those three headers (`Cache-Control`, `cdn-cache-control`, `cloudflare-cdn-cache-control`) are exactly the configuration surface for Cloudflare's Workers Caching product — and its cache key does NOT include the request host. developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/cache-keys: 'The request's host. The Worker's cache is keyed by path and query string, not the full URL' and, verbatim, 'If you genuinely need different cached responses for the same path on different hostnames — for example, white-labeled tenants where tenant-a.example.com/index and tenant-b.example.com/index must produce different content — the cache key does not do this for you automatically.' This is a multi-tenant Worker on one zone (`*/*` route on the SaaS zone, per the Cloudflare for SaaS worker-as-origin doc). Every tenant shares `/nl/`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/sitemaps/nl.xml`. The `vary` line explicitly forbids the only escape hatch.
fatal_flaws.correction: The design's own §2.3 ('the Worker must synthesise one robots.txt per Host header') and §2.4 (per-tenant sitemaps at a fixed path) become cross-tenant leaks the moment caching is enabled — a bakery serves the DJ's sitemap and robots.txt, and `bakkerij-jansen.mijnsaas.com/nl/` serves whichever tenant filled the entry first. Fix: add `Host` to `Vary` (the doc says 'All header names are honored... There is no allowlist'), or make the tenant part of the path, or front it with a gateway Worker that passes tenant id in `ctx.props` (which IS in the key). Also note `cache.enabled` is not in wrangler.toml today and requires Wrangler ≥ 4.69.0, so none of §4.11 is live yet — decide deliberately rather than discovering this in production.

fatal_flaws.claim: §6.5: the tenant's apex domain (`bakkerijjansen.nl`) becomes `sites.canonical_host`; every sitemap, JSON-LD @id, og:url and hreflang URL is rewritten to it; the 301 from the subdomain is 'forever' and the slug is 'never reused'.
fatal_flaws.why_wrong: Cloudflare for SaaS cannot serve a customer's zone apex on any non-Enterprise plan. The Plans table (developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/cloudflare-for-saas/plans/) lists 'Apex proxying/BYOIP' as Free: No / Pro: No / Business: No / Enterprise: Paid add-on, and 'Wildcard custom hostnames' as Enterprise-only. Pointing an apex at `cname.mijnsaas.com` requires the tenant's DNS provider to support CNAME flattening / ALIAS / ANAME at the zone apex. The target market — small local businesses in Europe on TransIP, Strato, OVH, Hostnet, one.com, IONOS default DNS — largely does not have that. The design has no `www` story, no fallback, and no DNS-instruction flow.
fatal_flaws.correction: Decide the canonical host shape before Phase 3, because §6.5 is explicitly a one-way door. Either (a) canonical = `www.bakkerijjansen.nl` with the apex handled by a redirect the tenant configures at their registrar, or (b) require tenants to move DNS to Cloudflare (a real onboarding cliff), or (c) budget Enterprise. Also budget the cost: `www` + apex are two custom hostnames, $0.10/mo each beyond the 100 included = ~$2,000/mo at 10k tenants, and the non-Enterprise ceiling of 50,000 custom hostnames caps the business at ~25,000 tenants.

fatal_flaws.claim: §4.9: 'Tenant sites: zero third-party origins. This is enforced by CSP, not by policy' with `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`; §6.6: 'detect injected <script>/<iframe> in user-editable fields (the CSP already blocks execution, but detect it and flag the account)'.
fatal_flaws.why_wrong: `'unsafe-inline'` is precisely the directive that permits inline scripts. An injected `<script>alert(1)</script>` in a business name, short_description, testimonial, alt text, or AI-written blog body executes. The stated defence does not exist. §6.6's sanitiser is described only for external links ('force rel=ugc nofollow noopener on every user-entered external link'), not for markup in text fields. The design also never says the renderer HTML-escapes tenant text — §3.8 carefully escapes JSON-LD (`<` → `<`) and says nothing about the HTML body.
fatal_flaws.correction: Stored XSS on a tenant site is bad on its own; combined with the host-less shared cache above it becomes one poisoned response served across tenants, and the tenant sites share an origin family with the dashboard's cookies unless the PSL entry has landed. Real fix: escape all tenant text at render, sanitise markup fields to a fixed allowlist on save AND on publish, and move to hashed inline scripts + `'strict-dynamic'` now rather than 'once the inline set is frozen' — the three inline blocks in §4.12 are already enumerated, so the hashes are computable today.

fatal_flaws.claim: §4.5 / §2.4 / §4.11 / §8: the publish pipeline transcodes AVIF/WebP/AV1/H.264, and pre-compresses every text asset with `brotli(bytes, 11)`, `zstd(bytes, 19)` and `gzip(bytes, 9)`, all inside `src/worker/publish/`.
fatal_flaws.why_wrong: None of this can run in a Worker. workerd's `CompressionStream` supports gzip/deflate only — no brotli, no zstd encoder — so quality-11 brotli and level-19 zstd mean WASM under a hard 128 MB memory limit (both plans) and against a 30 s default CPU budget (5 min max). The ffmpeg/SVT-AV1/libx264/avifenc/cwebp/pyftsubset commands in §4.5 and §4.8 are shell commands with no host named anywhere in the document or in wrangler.toml. `assets.ts` in the §8 layout is captioned 'AVIF/WebP/video transcode + br/zst/gz precompress + hashing' as if it were Worker code.
fatal_flaws.correction: This is the single largest hole in an otherwise detailed plan: there is no build compute in the architecture. Every tenant uploads a hero video that must be transcoded twice at two resolutions. Name the runtime — Cloudflare Containers, a Queue consumer feeding an external builder, or an external CI runner — and put it in wrangler.toml, because it changes the publish latency budget, the cost model, and the Phase-1 scaffold. Also drop zstd-19 and gzip-9: keep brotli-11 (offline) and identity.

fatal_flaws.claim: §6.3: a site stays `noindex` unless MinHash 5-gram Jaccard against the last 500 published sites in the same industry is ≤ 0.35, and every indexable page in the default locale has ≥ 300 words, a ≤65-char title and a ≥70-char meta description.
fatal_flaws.why_wrong: The 0.35 threshold is asserted, never calibrated against a single fixture. Two bakeries produced from the same ~40-component template system, the same industry preset, the same section ordering bucket, with the same structural boilerplate (opening-hours block, address block, 'Neem contact op', 'Over ons', footer, legal pages) will routinely exceed 0.35 Jaccard on 5-gram shingles of home body text — boilerplate is a large fraction of a small-business home page. The 300-word floor per indexable page is equally arbitrary: a contact page and an opening-hours page do not have 300 words of non-padding text, so the gate forces the generator to pad, which is itself the scaled-content signal the gate exists to prevent.
fatal_flaws.correction: The failure mode is silent and commercially fatal: the site ships, the customer pays €119.88, and Google never sees it. Worse, the remediation the dashboard shows ('voeg 2 eigen foto's en een langere bedrijfsomschrijving toe') cannot move a text-only MinHash at all — the advice doesn't match the gate that failed. Before this ships: generate 200 fixture sites across 10 industries, plot the actual Jaccard distribution, and set the threshold from data with a target false-positive rate. Make the gate report which check failed and give per-check remediation. And ship a manual override for support, because you will need it.

missing: Where the build compute lives. ffmpeg/SVT-AV1/avifenc/cwebp/pyftsubset/brotli-11 all appear in the design with no runtime that can host them, and no binding in wrangler.toml. This is a Phase-1 scaffold decision, not a Phase-3 detail.
A `www` vs apex decision and the DNS instructions each EU registrar needs. §6.5 is written entirely around the apex, which non-Enterprise Cloudflare for SaaS cannot serve.

404 / soft-404 policy. Nothing specifies what `/nl/bestaat-niet/` returns, what happens to a URL after a page is deleted in the editor (404? 410? redirect?), or how that interacts with §2.3's careful 404-vs-410 reasoning for whole sites.

Locale-mismatch handling. The five invariants in §1.1 never say what `/de/` does on a site whose `site_locales` has no `de` row — and §1.3 raises exactly this path as a real user journey ('the colleague lands on /de/menu/, which may not exist → 404').

A cost model. No number anywhere for Cloudflare for SaaS hostnames (~$2,000/mo at 10k tenants), R2 Class A/B operations, Workers requests, Analytics Engine data points, or claude-opus-5 tokens per generated site ($5/$25 per MTok), against €119.88/tenant/year. §6.3 specifies `effort: "high"` for the highest-token surface without costing it.

The true cost of adding a locale. §1.7 presents Italian as three INSERTs and 'zero code changes'. For an existing 10k-tenant base it is ~80,000 Opus 5 translation calls plus blog posts, plus a `src/shared/i18n/it.json`, plus `industry_translations` rows. Present it honestly or the first person to run it will be surprised by a five-figure invoice.

A rollback path for `index_state`. If the quality gate ships with a bug and flips 3,000 live sites to `noindex`, what reverses it, and what is the expected recrawl latency? The §7 trigger makes getting back to `index` require a passing `gate_result`, so a bad gate is self-locking.

Search Console ownership at 10k tenants. §6.5 steps 3 and 6 assume a verified per-tenant property and a Change of Address submission, but nothing owns that workflow, and a small business will not do it unaided.

Per-locale `alt` text generation for non-hero images. `media_assets.alt_text` exists as a JSON column but nothing in the SEO plan populates it, and Lighthouse a11y 100 requires alt on every content image.

Field CWV measurement that will actually return data. §4.13 plans a nightly CrUX pull for the top 200 tenant hosts; CrUX only publishes origins above a popularity threshold, which a bakery with 900 sessions/month will never clear. Without a first-party web-vitals beacon (not in the plan as a default), the p75 targets in §4 are unmeasurable for the population they are set for.
verdict: The SEO judgement in this document is genuinely strong — §3.6 (refusing to emit aggregateRating, with correct Google-policy, UCPD Annex I 23b/23c and Google Maps Platform reasoning), §2.2 (lastmod from a content hash, never a deploy), §2.3(c) (Disallow does not de-index; 200+noindex for 30 days, then 410), §1.3 (no geo-redirects), §3.4 (the openingHoursSpecification edge cases), §3.7 (author is the Organization, never a fabricated Person), §4.8 (self-hosted fonts, LG München I 3 O 17493/20), §5.1 (the banner is a function of what the site loads, asserted from the rendered tree), §6.1 and §6.6 (split the apex; no sitewide followed badge links; no cross-tenant directory) are all correct, well-argued, and are exactly the expensive-to-retrofit decisions a competitor gets wrong. I would build on that half unchanged. The infrastructure half does not survive contact with the platform. The caching architecture is the load-bearing failure: it conflates two different Cloudflare products, and the one whose configuration headers it actually sets keys its cache by path and query with the host explicitly excluded — which, on a Worker serving 10,000 white-labeled hostnames from one zone, means one tenant's HTML, robots.txt and sitemaps get served on every other tenant's domain. The `Vary` line forbids the documented fix. Alongside that: the entire asset pipeline (ffmpeg, AVIF, brotli-11) is specified as Worker code and cannot run in a Worker; the custom-domain migration is built on apex hostnames that non-Enterprise Cloudflare for SaaS cannot serve; the CSP is claimed to block script injection while carrying `'unsafe-inline'`; and the indexability gate ships an uncalibrated similarity threshold that will most likely noindex the paying customer base with remediation advice that cannot fix it. None of these are unfixable, and several are one-line fixes (`Vary: Host`, `imagesrcset` on the hero preload, reading `cf.clientAcceptEncoding`), but three of them — the canonical-host shape, the D1 single-database storage model, and where build compute lives — are architecture decisions that must be made before Phase 1 scaffolding freezes, not after. Take §1–§3, §5 and §6.1/§6.6 as written; send §4.5, §4.11, §6.3 and §6.5 back.
